title: Audit Log Access and Configuration
content:
# Audit Log Access and Configuration

CloudDash audit logs provide a detailed record of all user and system actions within your organization.

## What is Logged

- **User Actions**: Login/logout, dashboard CRUD, alert CRUD, integration changes, team member changes.
- **System Events**: Integration sync status, alert fires/resolutions, failed login attempts.
- **Admin Actions**: Role changes, billing changes, security setting modifications.
- **API Activity**: API key usage, endpoint access, rate limit events.

## Accessing Audit Logs

1. Navigate to **Settings > Security > Audit Log**.
2. Use filters to narrow results:
   - **Date range**: Select start and end dates.
   - **User**: Filter by specific user.
   - **Action type**: Filter by action category.
   - **Resource**: Filter by affected resource.
3. Click on any entry to view full details.

## Audit Log Retention

- **Starter**: No audit log access.
- **Pro**: 30 days of audit logs (view only).
- **Enterprise**: 365 days of audit logs (view + export).

## Exporting Audit Logs

Enterprise customers can export logs:
- **Manual Export**: Click **Export** on the Audit Log page. Choose CSV or JSON format.
- **API Export**: Use `GET /audit/logs?start=...&end=...` endpoint.
- **SIEM Integration**: Forward logs to your SIEM tool (Splunk, Datadog, Sumo Logic) via webhook.

## Compliance Use Cases

- **SOC 2**: Audit logs satisfy the monitoring and logging requirements.
- **GDPR**: Track all data access and modifications for compliance reporting.
- **Internal Audits**: Review who accessed what data and when.

## Important Notes

- Audit logs are immutable — they cannot be modified or deleted.
- Failed login attempts are always logged, regardless of plan.
- Audit log access requires Admin or custom role with Audit permission.
